title: Propionic acidaemia
summary: Propionic acidaemia means the body cannot break down some parts of protein and fat. Harmful substances can build up, often making a baby unwell in the first days of life.
inheritance_plain: It is inherited in an autosomal recessive way: a child is affected only if they get a changed copy of the same gene (PCCA or PCCB) from both parents.
carrier_meaning: A carrier has one changed copy. Carriers are healthy and usually do not know they are carriers until they are tested.
disease_meaning: A person with two changed copies has propionic acidaemia. It is managed for life with a special diet, medicines and close care from a specialist team, which also helps during illness.
screening: A carrier test uses a blood or saliva sample. It looks for the most common changes and cannot find every possible change.
suggested_questions: Someone in my family has propionic acidaemia. Could I be a carrier?

disease_short: Two changed copies. Managed for life by a specialist team with a special diet.
care: Specialist metabolic clinics, dietitians, genetic counselling and family support groups.
